posts.pinComment: If your agents ship volume but nobody scores misjudgment, comment OPS for the 7-question ops diagnostic (gates + taste loop).
posts.operatorNote: A0 operator-priority; multi-stage phone-booth WOW — example of post-score ship.
posts.text:
Clip below — what ships **after** the taste loop says repeat.

Most teams tune agents for output volume.
Almost nobody tunes for misjudgment.

I score every high-stakes deliverable:
Hook · Weirdness · Personality · Shareability · Cringe.

Then three questions:
1. What did the agent misjudge?
2. What rule gets updated?
3. What do we try differently next time?

This clip is the **repeat** path — mechanism held, execution earned the slot.

Controls:
owner on the scorecard,
log kill / mutate / repeat,
no schedule until reflection is written.

Daily AI pro tip:
Kill mechanisms, not moods. Log what failed as a rule, not a vibe.

posts.text:
Clip below — this one **passed** the creepy gate.

A lot of agent output dies in preview:
high wow, zero trust, frame-0 reads as horror before the caption explains anything.

So we kill the mechanism — not the mood board.

This clip made it through because surprise still shared an axis with the brand brief.

Practical tip:
if frame-0 feels uncanny on mute, it does not get a paragraph to recover.

posts.pinComment: If your team repeats the same agent failure every sprint, comment OPS for the triage doc I use before rollout.
posts.operatorNote: Batch 3 — identity-strength mutate candidate per FIA handoff; mechanism OK, execution regen.
posts.text:
Clip below — **mutate**, not a new strategy.

Fail once. Repeat forever — unless you log at mechanism level.

Weak axis.
Caption-only intelligence.
Identity drift on regen.

Different failure modes. Different log lines.

**kill** — mechanism is wrong.
**mutate** — mechanism is right, execution drift only.
**repeat** — scored and authorized to ship.

This run was a mutate: same concept transfer, tighter identity lock on regen.

Daily AI pro tip:
Ask "which mechanism failed?" before you ask "which model?"

posts.pinComment: If your hooks depend on AI-generated text in the image, comment OPS.
posts.operatorNote: Cinema-as-fabric concept — hook is visual motion, not readable model typography.
posts.text:
Clip below — the hook is motion, not AI lettering.

The worst agent outputs make you write an essay in the caption because frame zero failed.

Mobile does not read your explainer thread.

This brief succeeded because the WOW was cinematic — not a placard the model had to spell.

My rule:
blank shapes in the hero when text matters,
overlay I control in post,
bridge in copy — not in the diffusion call.

posts.text:
Clip below — surprise **with** overlap.

Random weird isn't creative.

Creative is surprise that still overlaps your operating truth.

Frame A: what the audience already reads.
Frame B: what domain you borrow.

They must share a **deep axis** with brand and operator taste.

This clip works because kinetic-fabric-as-sculpture and editorial fashion share the same axis — not because the tool picked a random domain.

Daily AI pro tip:
If you cannot name the shared axis in ten words, pause the run.

posts.pinComment: If you run parallel agents without canon docs, comment OPS.
posts.operatorNote: A0 surrealist object-flip — pack JSON + schedule manifest survived across sessions.
posts.text:
Clip below — exists because the **repo** remembered.

Session A had the context.
Session B had the deadline.

Parallel agents do not share chat.
They share canon: pack JSON, WOW rules, queue manifests.

This output was not rebuilt from a thread summary.
It was rebuilt from files the next lane could grep.

Practical tip:
if it is not in the repo, it did not happen for the next session.
